inputs.label: CPU PA7 Jumper J8 (firmware purpose unresolved)

physical.notes: The own-game schematic draws J8 from PIA11B PA7 pin 9 to ground, with a parallel RA4 4.7K pull-up to +5V. The CPU Jumper Table documents J8 installed for Phantom CPU Ver 2, ROMs 5B,5C, hence a grounded PA7 factory configuration. The inherited pia2a_r returns core_getDip(0)<<7: public configuration bit 0 at value 0 matches that grounded net, and value 1 matches the removed-jumper high level. This is a jumper position, not a physical DIP-switch bank. Its firmware purpose remains unresolved; DE_COMPORTS declares no Country port and the inherited Williams Country/W7 label is not game-specific evidence. Documented factory installation is not a claim about every surviving board.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP1516 = FLIP_SWNO(15,16) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

mechanisms.behavior: Upper-right ramp/hood pivots on its hinge and is moved by a rotary crank/25VAC motor through relay 14. Open 52 and Closed 53 are open midway, close before their respective endpoints and must not both close. The retained table starts closed (53 active), toggles direction in its animation on 14 pulses, and opens the collision path into the cavern. Its counter 0..60 is table tuning, not physical cam marks. Manual Organ Test pulses the relay while Start is held. Five fresh-state synthetic probes establish: startup with Closed 53 already active does not move; startup midway powers 14 until 53; completing 41-43 powers 14 until Open 52, then a timed return stops on 53. With both host limit inputs held open, three automatic attempts each stop after about six host-clock seconds rather than running indefinitely. In Organ Test, Start held produces repeated short pulses independent of those limits. Candidate cam width and powered speed were varied; neither is a physical measurement.
mechanisms.label: Raising Organ and Cavern

mechanisms.behavior: Two ball-presence contacts in one left-side stack; bsSaucer slots 1/2 assert 28/29, capacity two, one ball released by 27. Its mouth feeds the left wire ramp through a separate VPX raise helper; helper Kicker1 is not another physical actuator. Default empty. Exact physical sensor offsets remain unlocated.
mechanisms.label: Two-ball Left VUK / Lock

mechanisms.behavior: Outhole 10 is recovered by 25 into the three-ball trough 11/12/13; 26 feeds the manual shooter lane 14. The table starts three balls in its stack (13,12,11 active), destroys drain balls into that model and maps 25 to its stack input. The two physical coils remain distinct. Script ballreleasehack is a recreation workaround, not physical wiring.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball Trough and Outhole

mechanisms.behavior: Below-playfield subway delivers a ball to occupied switch 36; 28 ejects it upward into its return path. The table clears 36 as it destroys/recreates/raises the ball before kicking it. Default empty. These teleport/height increments do not prescribe physical tuning.
mechanisms.label: Top Super VUK

mechanisms.behavior: A ball through the spring-return hanging Magic Mirror enters the subway at 45 and reaches the right VUK contact 44. Output 29 ejects it back to the surface/return route. 45 is a ball-path switch, not directly actuated by 29. The table's BottomVUK/teleport helpers simplify this path; default empty.
mechanisms.label: Right Super VUK / Magic Mirror Return

mechanisms.behavior: The left outlane ball switch 17 reports a ball. When ROM rules allow, 16 fires the kickback to return that ball to play; otherwise it drains. The script fires/pulls back Plunger1. A sensed ball does not mechanically force a coil command.
mechanisms.label: Left-outlane Laser Kick

mechanisms.behavior: Special SP3 drives the left sling 23-800 coil; the manual separately lists trigger and matrix-point contacts. A physical trigger reflex acts while enabled. PinMAME alpha omits ssSw synthesis, so the VPX sling collision both rebounds the ball and pulses 21.
mechanisms.label: Left Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Special SP5 drives the right sling 23-800 coil with distinct trigger and point contacts; enabled hardware reflex. The VPX sling collision supplies physics and pulses 22 rather than awaiting an alpha special callback.
mechanisms.label: Right Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Special SP4, 23-800 coil, skirt/trigger and point contact on the left bumper. The retained Bumper1 pulses 46 and performs its own recoil/lighting.
mechanisms.label: Left Pop Bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Special SP2, 23-800 coil, skirt/trigger and point contact on the lower center bumper. The retained Bumper3 pulses 47; object numbering is not switch numbering.
mechanisms.label: Center Pop Bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Special SP1, 23-800 coil, skirt/trigger and point contact on the right bumper. The retained Bumper2 pulses 48.
mechanisms.label: Right Pop Bumper

mechanisms.behavior: One physical 23-900 coil on the solid-state flipper board drives the left bat. The normally-open cabinet microswitch writes public 84; core copies it to 15 and fabricates 47/48 while enabled 23. EOS/power/hold hardware must not be reconstructed as independent CPU outputs.
mechanisms.label: Left Cabinet-wired Flipper

mechanisms.behavior: One physical 23-900 coil on the solid-state flipper board drives the right bat. The normally-open cabinet microswitch writes public 82; core copies it to 16 and fabricates 45/46 while enabled 23. PinMAME models no physical EOS contact here.
mechanisms.label: Right Cabinet-wired Flipper
